column1: accommodation|A place to live or stay.|The agency provides temporary accommodation near the station.
tenant|Someone who rents a home from its owner.|Each tenant receives a copy of the agreement.
landlord|The owner of a property that someone rents.|Please ask the landlord to repair the heater.
rent|Money paid regularly to use someone else's property.|The rent includes water but not electricity.
deposit|Money held as security against damage or unpaid charges.|Your deposit will be returned after the inspection.
furnished|Provided with furniture.|We need a furnished flat for three months.
flat|A set of rooms forming a home within a building.|Our flat is above a small grocery shop.
apartment|A home consisting of rooms within a larger building.|The apartment has a shared laundry room.
house|A building in which people live.|The house is within walking distance of the school.
household|The people who live together in one home.|Each household receives two recycling bins.
resident|A person who lives in a particular place.|Every resident needs a permit to park here.
neighbour|Someone who lives close to you.|Our neighbour collects our post when we travel.
roommate|Someone who shares a room with you.|My roommate works early in the morning.
flatmate|Someone who shares a flat with you.|Each flatmate pays an equal share of the bills.
suburb|A residential area outside a city's centre.|The suburb has a direct bus service downtown.
neighbourhood|The area around where people live.|There is a community garden in our neighbourhood.
address|The details showing where a home or building is.|Please provide your new address before moving.
postcode|Letters or numbers identifying a postal area.|Include the postcode on the delivery form.
property|A building or piece of land that someone owns.|The agent will show you the property tomorrow.
entrance|The place where you go into a building.|Visitors should use the main entrance.
exit|The way out of a building or area.|Keep the emergency exit clear at all times.
hallway|A passage connecting rooms in a building.|Please do not leave bicycles in the hallway.
staircase|A set of stairs joining different floors.|The staircase is being cleaned this afternoon.
lift|A machine that carries people between floors.|The lift is unavailable during maintenance.
balcony|An outdoor platform attached to an upper floor.|Do not hang heavy objects from the balcony.
garden|Land beside a home where plants are grown.|The tenant is responsible for keeping the garden tidy.
garage|A building or space for keeping a car.|The garage can also be used for storage.
driveway|A private route between a road and a building.|Please keep the driveway free for deliveries.
basement|A floor or room below ground level.|Personal storage is available in the basement.
attic|A space directly below the roof.|The attic has been insulated to reduce heat loss.
roof|The top covering of a building.|A contractor will repair the roof next week.
ceiling|The upper inside surface of a room.|There is a damp patch on the ceiling.
wall|A vertical structure enclosing or dividing rooms.|Ask permission before painting a wall.
floor|The lower surface of a room.|The kitchen floor becomes slippery when wet.
carpet|A thick fabric covering for a floor.|The carpet must be professionally cleaned before departure.
curtain|Fabric hung over a window for privacy or shade.|A thick curtain helps keep the bedroom warm.
window|An opening with glass that lets in light.|Please close the window when the heating is on.
door|A movable barrier at a room's entrance.|The front door locks automatically after closing.
lock|A device that secures a door or container.|Report a broken lock to the caretaker immediately.
key|An object used to open a lock.|Leave the spare key with the property manager.
heating|A system that keeps a building warm.|The heating switches off automatically at midnight.
boiler|Equipment that heats water for a building.|The boiler needs its annual safety inspection.
radiator|Equipment that releases heat into a room.|Keep furniture away from the radiator.
damp|Unwanted moisture in a building or material.|Please report any signs of damp behind furniture.
mould|A fungus that grows on damp surfaces.|The landlord arranged treatment for mould on the ceiling.
leak|An unwanted escape of water or gas.|Turn off the water if you notice a leak.
plumber|A person who installs or repairs water pipes.|A plumber will replace the leaking tap.
electrician|A person who installs or repairs electrical systems.|Only an electrician should repair the damaged socket.
socket|A fixed fitting into which an electrical plug goes.|Do not connect too many appliances to one socket.
appliance|A machine used for a household task.|Report any faulty appliance supplied with the flat.
fridge|A machine that keeps food cool.|The shared fridge is cleaned every Friday.
freezer|A machine that keeps food frozen.|Please label your food before using the freezer.
oven|An enclosed appliance used for baking or roasting.|The oven must be cleaned at the end of the tenancy.
cooker|An appliance used to prepare food with heat.|The new cooker has an electric hob.
kettle|A container used to boil water.|A kettle is provided in the communal kitchen.
laundry|Clothes or other fabric items that need washing.|Do not leave your laundry in the shared machines.
detergent|A substance used for washing clothes or surfaces.|Residents must supply their own laundry detergent.
sink|A fixed bowl with a drain and water supply.|Please do not pour cooking oil down the sink.
tap|A device controlling the flow of water.|The bathroom tap continues to drip after closing.
shower|Equipment that sprays water for washing your body.|The shower is shared by three residents.
bathroom|A room containing washing and toilet facilities.|Please leave the bathroom clean after use.
bedroom|A room used for sleeping.|The larger bedroom faces the courtyard.
living room|A room used for relaxing and spending time together.|Visitors may use the shared living room until ten.
dining room|A room used for eating meals.|The dining room can seat six people.
furniture|Movable items such as tables, chairs and beds.|Check the condition of the furniture on arrival.
wardrobe|A cupboard for hanging clothes.|There is a built-in wardrobe in each bedroom.
shelf|A flat surface used for storing items.|Please secure the shelf before placing books on it.
drawer|A sliding storage compartment in furniture.|Keep the appliance instructions in the kitchen drawer.
mattress|The soft padded part of a bed.|The damaged mattress will be replaced this week.
bedding|Sheets, blankets and other bed coverings.|Short-term residents must bring their own bedding.
towel|Absorbent fabric used for drying things.|Please hang each wet towel where it can dry.
repair|Work done to fix something damaged or broken.|The repair should take less than an hour.
condition|The state that something is in.|Photograph the condition of the rooms when you arrive.
damage|Physical harm that reduces something's usefulness or value.|Report accidental damage to the property manager.
shared|Used by more than one person or household.|The building has a shared courtyard.
private|For use by one person or group only.|The bedroom has a private bathroom.
spacious|Having plenty of room.|We are looking for a spacious flat for our family.
affordable|Not too expensive for the person paying.|The council helps families find affordable housing.
convenient|Easy to use or suitable for your needs.|This location is convenient for the evening bus.
accessible|Easy to reach, enter or use.|The ground-floor flat is accessible to wheelchair users.
tenancy|The arrangement allowing someone to rent a home.|Our tenancy begins on the first of June.
lease|A contract allowing use of a property for a period.|Read the lease before signing it.
premises|The building and land used by a household or business.|Smoking is not allowed anywhere on the premises.
insulation|Material that reduces heat loss through a building.|Better insulation should lower our energy bills.
ventilation|The movement of fresh air through a building.|Good ventilation helps prevent damp in the bathroom.
plumbing|The pipes and fittings that carry water in a building.|The plumbing will be checked before you move in.
renovation|Work that improves or restores a building.|The kitchen renovation will begin after we move out.
inventory|A list of the items supplied with a property.|Check the inventory before accepting the keys.
wear and tear|Damage caused gradually by normal use.|Ordinary wear and tear is allowed under the agreement.
notice period|The advance warning required before ending an arrangement.|The tenancy has a four-week notice period.
eviction|The legal removal of someone from a rented property.|The letter explained the reason for the proposed eviction.
renewal|The extension of an agreement for another period.|Contact the agent to discuss your lease renewal.
occupancy|The use of a building as a place to live or work.|The flat is ready for occupancy from September.
residential|Used mainly as a place for people to live.|Please drive slowly through the residential area.
relocation|The process of moving to a new place.|Our employer will help with the cost of relocation.
unfurnished|Not provided with furniture.|The unfurnished apartment has a cooker but no beds.
vacancy|A place or position that is available.|The residence has one vacancy from Monday.
utilities|Services such as water, electricity and gas.|The advertised price does not include utilities.
maintenance|Work that keeps a building or equipment in good condition.|Routine maintenance takes place on weekday mornings.
inspection|A careful check of a property's condition.|We will arrange an inspection before returning your deposit.
